WPG.head: The Jets have a hill to climb
WPG.body: Even though Winnipeg has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and gets Hanifin back. The Jets can pull it off if they keep shots to a minimum.

VGK.head: The Golden Knights have a lot going for them
VGK.body: Even though Winnipeg has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and gets Hanifin back. The Jets’ way back in is keeping shots to a minimum.

story.head: The Golden Knights are searching for answers
paras: The Jets (11-9-3) beat the Islanders 4-3 in overtime on Thursday, while the Golden Knights are winless in four (0-1-3). Going in, the Knights are second in the Pacific (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Jets sixth in the Central (tied for 15th).
This season, the Golden Knights have outscored teams 79-68, but only 49-46 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 24-16.

The Golden Knights (2nd) and the Jets (3rd) both create chances on the penalty kill. The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st) and have one of the league’s best penalty kills (2nd). The Jets rarely ice the puck (5th). They also get their shots through to the net (4th), and their knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. The Golden Knights’ power play (4th) could do real damage against the Jets’ penalty kill (24th).

Jack Eichel (9 G / 20 A / 29 P in 24 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, and Mark Stone (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 24 GP) has a team-high eleven goals. Mark Scheifele (7 G / 22 A / 29 P in 23 GP) leads the Jets in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games. Kyle Connor (18 G / 10 A / 28 P in 23 GP) has a team-high 18 goals, tied for third in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games.
Carter Hart (6-4-2 / .888 SV% in 12 GS) is expected to start for Vegas, and Stuart Skinner (7-5-3 / .883 SV% in 16 GS) for Winnipeg.

At home, Scott Arniel likes to send Koepke, Barron and Zhilkin out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Gatcomb, Dowd and Bowman. Elsewhere, the Golden Knights usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.
